item.title: US-Bangla Airlines consecutively achieves ‘Best Domestic Airline of the Year-2026’
item.description:
US-Bangla Airlines has been awarded the "Best Domestic Airline of the Year-2026" by The Bangladesh Monitor, a fortnightly travel magazine in Bangladesh, in recognition of enhancing domestic air connectivity and maintaining stability in the country's civil aviation sector.
At the award ceremony, US-Bangla also received recognition as the Best Wage Earner Friendly Airline, Best Short Haul Airline, Best Airport Service (Domestic), Popular Airline Brand in Bangladesh, Outstanding Community Service, Best Regional Airline, and Best Improved Airline.
Shafiqul Islam, head of sales at US-Bangla Airlines, received the "Best Domestic Airline of the Year-2026" award from chief guest Nasser Rahman, MP.
The awards were officially presented on November 8, 2026, at Crown Plaza Dhaka Airport.
Among other distinguished guests present at the event were Nurunnahar Chowdhury, secretary of Civil Aviation and Tourism, and Kazi Wahidul Alam, editor of The Bangladesh Monitor.
Additionally, US-Bangla Airlines received Gold awards in the categories of Best Airport Service (Domestic), Best Popular Airline Brand in Bangladesh, and Best Improved Airline, and Silver awards in the Best Short Haul, Best Wage Earner Friendly Airline, Best Outstanding Connectivity Service, and Best Regional Airline categories.
These awards from various categories were received from the guests by AKM Junaid, director of customer service; Md Kamrul Islam, general manager of Public Relations; and Iqbal Ahmed, manager of central reservations at US-Bangla Airlines.
Following the Monitor Airline of the Year 2026 awards, Mohammed Abdullah Al Mamun, managing director of US-Bangla Airlines, stated: "This recognition for US-Bangla Airlines is a reflection of the trust placed in us by our passengers. Such accolades pledge US-Bangla Airlines to do even better moving forward."
US-Bangla Airlines was previously honored with the 'Best Domestic Airline' award by The Bangladesh Monitor in 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, and 2015.

item.title: Police vehicle vandalised, activities-banned AL leader taken away in handcuffs
item.description:
A group of people stopped a police vehicle in Jaintiapur, Sylhet, and snatched a leader of Awami League, whose activities are banned, while he was handcuffed. They also vandalised the police vehicle.

The incident took place on Monday night in the Koricher Pul area of Haripur in the upazila of Sylhet.

Police later conducted a drive and detained three people on suspicion of involvement in the incident.

The Awami League (activities banned) leader is Zakaria Mahmud from Hemu Haudpara village in the Haripur area. . He is the deputy office secretary of Jaintiapur upazila Awami League and a former joint general secretary of the district Chhatra League.

According to police sources, Zakaria Mahmud was detained by police from the Station area of Haripur Bazar in Jaintiapur at around 7:30pm on Monday.

While he was being taken to the police station, several people blocked the police vehicle with a pickup truck in the Koricher Pul area of the Sylhet–Tamabil highway, about one kilometre from the market. They vandalised the police vehicle and took Zakaria away while he was still handcuffed.

Jaintiapur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mahbubur Rahman Molla said five cases had been filed against Zakaria at the police station. He was detained on Monday night. While he was being taken to the police station, the police vehicle was blocked and the detainee was snatched away along with his handcuffs. Police later conducted a drive at night and detained three people involved in the incident.

OC Mahbubur Rahman Molla further said that operations were underway to arrest Zakaria and the others involved in snatching him away.

item.title: Sonali Bank to offer scholarships to students, who can apply?
item.description:
Sonali Bank PLC will provide educational scholarships for 2025 under its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programme. Underprivileged and meritorious students across the country can apply for the scholarships.

Online applications opened today, Sunday (8 November 2026), and will remain open until 27 November 2026. Each selected student will receive a one-time grant of Tk 15,000.

According to a notice published on Sonali Bank’s website, interested students must apply online within the stipulated period. Further details about the scholarship are available on the bank’s CSR-related website.

Eligibility criteria

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

a. Students who passed the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) or equivalent examination in 2025 and are currently studying at the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) or equivalent level can apply.

b. Students who passed the HSC or equivalent examination in 2025 and are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or equivalent programme can also apply.

c. For underprivileged and meritorious students studying at the HSC or equivalent level, the minimum GPA requirements in the SSC or equivalent examination are as follows:

- General students: GPA 5.00

- Children of freedom fighters: GPA 4.50

- Students from ethnic minority communities: GPA 4.50

- Students with physical disabilities and third-gender students: GPA 3.50

d. For students pursuing undergraduate or equivalent studies, the minimum GPA requirements in the HSC or equivalent examination are as follows:

- General students: GPA 5.00

- Children of freedom fighters: GPA 4.50

- Students from ethnic minority communities: GPA 4.50

- Students with physical disabilities and third-gender students: GPA 3.50

e. Only students from the following categories can apply: underprivileged students, students from ethnic minority communities, orphans, students with disabilities, and children of financially disadvantaged Bir Muktijoddhas (gallantry-awarded freedom fighters). The monthly income of their parents or guardians must not exceed Tk 15,000, excluding freedom fighter allowances. Children of financially solvent families do not need to apply.

Important application dates

Interested students can apply from today, Sunday (8 November 2026). They must complete and submit the online application form through Sonali Bank’s website by 27 November 2026.

item.title: Grenade-like objects found at Rajshahi airport, minister evacuated through rear gate
item.description:
Law enforcement agencies have reported the recovery of two grenade-like objects from Hazrat Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi. Authorities recovered the objects from an area in front of the airport’s main gate at around 11:00 am today, Tuesday.

At the same time, Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku arrived at the airport on a flight. After authorities discovered the grenade-like objects near the main entrance, security personnel escorted the minister out through the rear gate as a precaution.

Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Airport police station in Rajshahi, Robiul Islam, confirmed the incident to Prothom Alo.

Police said they had moved the two grenade-like objects to a secure location. They will take the necessary measures after examining them.

OC Robiul Islam further said a local resident alerted airport police to the two grenade-like objects at 10:55 am. Police cordoned off the area immediately.

Meanwhile, the minister arrived at the airport on a flight at 10:50 am. He was inside the airport’s VIP lounge at the time. After officials informed him about the grenade-like objects, security personnel escorted him out through the airport’s rear gate as a precaution. He later left for Bogura by road.

Rajshahi Police spokesperson and Deputy Commissioner Gaziur Rahman said the authorities would take the necessary measures after examining the two objects.

2 crude bombs recovered from Dhanmondi 32, note found nearby
item.description:
Police have recovered two unexploded crude bombs from in front of the demolished residence of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman at Dhanmondi 32 in the capital.

A handwritten note was also found nearby, bearing the words, “Joy Bangla, Projonmo-71”. The bombs were later defused.

The bombs were recovered at around 11:45am today, Tuesday. Dhanmondi police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Muhammad Imdadul Islam Toyeb confirmed the information to Prothom Alo.

At around the same time, two unexploded crude bombs were found at a location beside City College in Dhanmondi. The bombs were subsequently recovered and defused.

OC Imdadul Islam told Prothom Alo that two people came to Dhanmondi 32 and left the two bombs there before leaving the scene.

They could not detonate the bombs because of the police's heightened security measures.

Similarly, unidentified individuals left two bombs near City College and walked away.

Dhanmondi police said several people spotted the two bombs in front of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's demolished residence at Dhanmondi 32 and informed the police. Officers cordoned off the area and subsequently called in the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Bomb Disposal Unit. The unit arrived and recovered and defused the bombs.

Regarding the note, OC Imdadul Islam said it was found near the bombs recovered from Dhanmondi 32. It read, “Joy Bangla, Projonmo-71”.

The OC said police were investigating whether the note was connected to the bombs.

item.title: “Allah, I have entrusted my son to Your path; Show him mercy.”
item.description:
The 14-year-old boy is in the ICU. Outside, his mother prays for him. She says, “Allah, I entrusted my son to Your path and sent him to study Your holy book. You alone, have mercy on him.”

Sonia Akter was seen standing outside the ICU on the fourth floor of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in the capital on Tuesday afternoon. Her son’s name is Azizul Islam Siam.

Azizul, who was injured in a fire at a madrasa in the Signboard area of Fatullah, Narayanganj, has been brought to Dhaka. His mother told Prothom Alo, “He is my only child. As my firstborn, I wanted to raise him as a Hafiz of the Quran. That is why I enrolled him at Jamia Ashrafia Madrasa, right next to our home. Siam became a Hafiz at just 14. He has devoted himself to reciting Allah’s holy book. Allah, I pray to You: he has been studying Your holy book. Have mercy on him and let my son recover.”

The Fire Service said a fire broke out at Jamia Ashrafia Madrasa at around 1 am early Monday. Students admitted to the hospital said the fire started in the library and office rooms on the second floor of the madrasah's five-storey building. Around 250 students used to stay in the building overnight. 

The fire spread through the two rooms, which covered an area of approximately 4,000 square feet. Three units from the Kanchpur Modern Fire Station and two from the Shibu Market Modern Fire Station took part in extinguishing the blaze. Electricity went out immediately after the fire broke out. As the students made their way downstairs using the staircase, they all became ill from inhaling the smoke. Later that night, they were brought to the Burn Institute in Dhaka. They do not know what caused the fire.

Sonia Akter said the madrasa was just a two- to three-minute walk from their home. She was asleep when the fire broke out at night. She woke up after hearing screams and commotion following the outbreak of the fire.

The mother said, “My son has been placed in the ICU. They have put an oxygen mask on him. I went to see him once this morning. Siam's father lives in Saudi Arabia. He returned there on the 4th of last month. He keeps calling to ask about our son. I don't know what to tell him. The doctors are telling me not to worry. But how can a mother stop worrying? Allah, please have mercy on him.”

Sultan Mahmud Sikder, the hospital's resident surgeon, told Prothom Alo that four of the admitted patients were in critical condition. They had been placed in the ICU for close monitoring and treatment. Siam was among them and was receiving mechanical ventilation.

The doctor said a total of 79 students had so far sought medical attention following the fire. However, none of them had any visible burn injuries. Almost all had fallen ill to varying degrees from smoke inhalation, which had affected their respiratory tracts.

He added that 63 injured students had been admitted to the hospital for treatment and observation. The remaining 16 had received the necessary treatment and been discharged. A medical board comprising 10–12 doctors had been formed to oversee their treatment.

item.title: Kaleidoscope of teen times
item.description:
Teenage years are often described as the golden years of life, a time where one is carefree, no responsibilities, just studies, fun and freedom. Is that how it really is, especially in the present day where pressures appear from all directions?

 The late teen years are characterised by a lot of stress and anxiety. There is immense pressure to do well in school. After that, you are expected to craft a compelling college application, achieve near-perfect standardised test scores and create an impressive extracurricular profile. The transition to becoming an adult is not always smooth. The realization that soon we will be on our own and no longer have our parents at our disposal, making all the decisions for us, hits hard.

Maybe a sneak peek into a typical day in my life will give a picture of what life is really like for a teenager.

 As an 11th grader in high school, my day starts at around 7 am in the morning. I wake up, get dressed, pack my bag, grab a quick breakfast and leave the house within 7:30 am. I am at the school premises by 7:45. I check my routine for the respective day and go to the assigned classrooms. During breaks, I like to hang out with my friend. We go to the library, the canteen and enjoy walks around the beautiful campus. After I am done with my classes for the day I go back home. But I’m not done for the day yet! My coaching classes extend from early afternoon to late evening. By the end of the classes, I feel exhausted. If I do not have any more homework left, I mostly spend the rest of the day chatting with my friends online or watching reality shows and listening to my favorite music. I like to have a very light dinner and then hit the bed by 12 am.

More or less, this is what a day in the life of most people my age looks like. But of course, there are exceptions.

Technology to the rescue!

 It is indubitable that advancements in technology have played a pivotal role in crafting the silhouette of modern lives. Technology has seeped into every aspect of life ranging from education to healthcare and more. Studying has become a lot simpler with the help of new AI tools that can act as our personal mentors.

 In stark contrast, students in previous generations had to heavily rely on limited resources such as textbooks and teachers for academic support. While that is still prevalent, we as students can now access innumerable resources online such as notes and video lectures that can prove to be tremendously valuable especially during last minute exam prep and assignment deadlines. However, it is also important to note that the superfluous use of technology can strip away our creativity and create a state of dependency that can be difficult to overcome.

Social media syndrome

 Moreover, the detrimental effects of social media almost have no bounds. Exposure to highly curated social media content can have negative psychological consequences for young adults specifically. Seeing perfectly polished Instagram posts gives birth to the misconception that other people are way ahead of us in life. Doomscrolling can foster unhealthy social comparisons and diminish self-esteem, potentially contributing to depression and other mental health problems.

 It becomes increasingly difficult to admit the fact that it is unfair and unreasonable to compare our behind-the-scenes with someone else’s highlight reel.

A different world

 Let’s take a moment to look around us. Countless underprivileged children are deprived of their fundamental rights and are forced into employment at an early age simply to make ends meet. For them, education is a distant dream that remains beyond their reach. Although Bangladesh has made notable progress in other areas, child labour still remains ubiquitous.

As we transition from youth to young adulthood, we begin planning our higher education, careers and future aspirations. However, let us also pause to ask ourselves an important question: What can we do to make a difference in the lives of those less fortunate than us?

item.title: She herself wants to return, she'll say extradite me, I see no complications: Zahed Ur Rahman
item.description:
Since ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who is currently in India, wants to return to the country herself, the government foresees no complications under extradition law, Information and Broadcasting Adviser to the prime minister, Zahed Ur Rahman, has said.

The information adviser made these remarks today, Tuesday in response to journalists' questions at a regular briefing held at the Secretariat to report on government activities.

If Sheikh Hasina wants to return, govt will act under extradition treaty

Zahed Ur Rahman said, “We want to extradite her. We want to bring her back... Now, she wants to return herself. That means she does not even need to go to the court. She will simply say 'extradite me'... Therefore, regarding the legal process or legal complexities being talked about concerning extradition, I, at least, see none.”

The information adviser remarked that the government wants the convicted accused extradited, and the Indian government must allow this to happen, adding that Indian government should have no reason for concern at this point. He stated, “Because the person who is to be extradited wants to come back herself. So, we no longer believe there is any legal issue.”

Sheikh Hasina's new passport: Delhi receives email, forwards it to Dhaka

A Reuters report on Monday revealed that ousted Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina has applied for a new passport and National Identity Card (NID) to return home. She submitted the application to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, India, according to a letter obtained by Reuters.

According to Reuters, this is the first such application Sheikh Hasina has made since fleeing to India on 5 August 2024 amid student-led mass protests. This step is being viewed as the clearest indication yet of her plan to return to Bangladesh, which she intends to do this coming December.

item.title: Stick-wielding BCL activists block road near Padma Bridge, explode crude bombs late at night
item.description:
Leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned in the country, and the banned Chhatra League held a demonstration by blocking the road while wielding "logi" (wooden poles) and "boitha" (oars) in front of the toll plaza at the Zajira end of the Padma Bridge in the small hours of Tuesday.

They allegedly exploded several crude bombs and vandalised trucks during the incident, which occurred between 1:30 am and 2:30 am in the Naodoba area of Zajira.

Traffic was halted on the Dhaka–Bhanga Expressway for nearly an hour, stranding hundreds of vehicles across the bridge and in surrounding areas.

Traffic returned to normal after police and highway police arrived at the scene and dispersed the activists. Police confirmed that no individuals have been detained so far in connection with the incident.

According to local and police sources, around 700 to 800 people gathered in the Naodoba area at around 1:30 am. Among them were leaders, activists, and supporters of the Awami League and Chhatra League.

At one point, carrying poles and oars, they took up positions on the expressway in front of the toll plaza and began demonstrating. During this time, a series of crude bombs exploded in quick succession. Police also reported that two trucks parked on the road were vandalised.

The demonstration brought traffic to a complete standstill, affecting vehicles bound for Dhaka from the south-western region as well as those heading towards the south-west from Dhaka.

Later, members of Padma Bridge South police station, Shibchar Highway police station, and district police dispersed the demonstrators.

The incident took place near the Padma Bridge South police station, the military cantonment, the bridge’s service area, and the toll plaza. The late-night blockade and crude bomb explosions in a highly critical zone sparked widespread panic among passengers.

Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Shibchar Highway police station, Enamul Hasan, told Prothom Alo that additional police personnel, alongside members from Padma Bridge South police station and highway police, conducted a joint operation to clear the activists of the banned organisations from the road.

The banned Chhatra League had announced a nationwide blockade programme for today, 10 November, via Facebook.

Centred around this programme, information of activists gathering in various parts of Shariatpur began circulating from the previous day. Police had conducted a raid in the Naodoba area on Monday evening, seizing 500 packets of khichuri from a commercial establishment. Later, a protest march was organised in the area by the Shariatpur District Jubo Dal, youth wing of ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

During the late-night demonstration, Mohsin Madbor, convenor of Shariatpur District unit Chhatra League, was seen delivering a speech.

A video of his speech circulated on Facebook, in which he was heard declaring that any interference by the BNP with their programmes would be resisted.

item.title: Foreign relations should be pursued in our own interests, on our own terms
item.description:
Whenever the issue of a new port, major investment, or defence cooperation arises in Bangladesh, a familiar set of concerns takes centre stage: What will India think? How will China react? Will the United States be displeased? These are not irrelevant questions. But when the reactions of others are given priority over our own needs, foreign policy can gradually lose sight of its own destination. Bangladesh needs to rethink this approach as it looks to the future.

These concerns have a real basis. Bangladesh shares deep geographical, riverine, border, and security ties with India. China is an important partner in infrastructure, manufacturing, and investment. The United States matters because of its influence on exports, technology, and the international order. As a result, closer ties with one country may arouse suspicion in another.

Taking this reality into account, Bangladesh needs an international posture that not only maintains relations with major powers but also expands cooperation with other partners to strengthen our capabilities and freedom of decision-making. Preserving multiple viable options, even under pressure, is what makes sovereignty meaningful in practice.

In the language of international relations, two concepts frequently arise in this context: ‘hedging’ and ‘bandwagoning’. Hedging means managing risks and preserving alternatives by maintaining relations with multiple powers amid uncertainty. Bandwagoning means strategically aligning with a powerful state in pursuit of security or other benefits. The former requires diplomatic skill and credibility, while the latter, despite offering certain immediate advantages, can constrain freedom of decision-making in the long run.

The question for Bangladesh is which approach will strengthen its capacity to make independent decisions. Hedging, too, can fail. Offering assurances to one side today and making contradictory commitments to another tomorrow can breed distrust. Nor does postponing necessary decisions simply to keep everyone happy qualify as hedging. Effective hedging rests on clearly defined national interests, consistent policies, and preparedness for crises. What Bangladesh needs is ‘strategic autonomy’ built on these foundations: the doors to cooperation will remain open, but no partner will be granted an unwritten veto over our decisions.

To achieve this independence, Bangladesh must first determine which capabilities will be essential over the next two decades: diversified exports, reliable energy, skilled employment, technological advancement, climate resilience, and maritime security. The next question should be: which country is best suited to meet each of these needs as a partner? This map of national priorities should determine the hierarchy of our international relationships.

A needs-based approach also requires clear principles for managing relations with India, China, and the United States. There is neither a possibility nor a need to make the volume of trade, investment, or security cooperation with these countries equal. What must be equal is the standard by which these relationships are managed: mutual respect, transparent agreements, sovereign decision-making, and reasonable accountability. India's importance is distinct because of geographical realities; China's role in industrialisation is different; and the United States serves different needs in terms of markets and technology. Bangladesh must build its relationships by recognising these differences, without placing any state in the position of a permanent guardian.

In the case of India, Bangladesh must manage cooperation and unresolved issues simultaneously. While expanding opportunities in connectivity, electricity, and trade, it must also pursue regular, evidence-based discussions on river water sharing, border fatalities, and barriers to market access. Cooperation cannot come at the cost of silently accepting unresolved problems. At the same time, suspending all cooperation because of existing disputes would be self-defeating.

World changing with BRICS: What Bangladesh should do

The same logic applies to relations with China. The scale of infrastructure needs does not make every major project necessary or worthwhile. Beyond interest rates, Bangladesh must assess repayment periods, foreign exchange risks, project revenues, maintenance costs, and local employment opportunities. The value of the relationship will increase if Chinese investment can be linked to Bangladesh's industrial capacity, supply chains, and export diversification. The completion of construction alone is not a measure of success; the real test is how much that infrastructure contributes to domestic productivity.

Relations with the United States must likewise be freed from the narrow pursuit of political approval. Bangladesh needs long-term programmes focused on export markets, higher education, research, technology, and responsible investment. Treating issues such as labour rights and good governance merely as external pressure means missing opportunities to improve our own institutions. Deepening economic ties with one country does not mean taking a strategic position against another.

One important way to make these three relationships sustainable is to expand Bangladesh's network of capable partners beyond them. Here, ‘alternatives’ do not mean replacing India with Japan or choosing Europe instead of China. Rather, they mean ensuring that the country does not come to a standstill if a particular market, financier, technology source, or supplier becomes unavailable. Bargaining power comes not so much from the number of relationships a country maintains as from the availability of viable alternatives. One must be deferential when facing a closed door; having several doors open expands the freedom to choose.

What Bangladesh can gain from PM's Japan visit

Japan offers a practical example of this potential. Through JICA's Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative, infrastructure, the investment climate, and connectivity have been considered as interconnected priorities. The lesson for Bangladesh is that ports must be linked to industrial zones, a skilled workforce, and domestic suppliers. Similar partnerships can also be explored with South Korea in manufacturing technology and technical training. When cooperation builds production-related knowledge alongside financing, it becomes a lasting national asset.

Alongside productive capacity, Bangladesh also needs guaranteed access to markets. The European Union, therefore, cannot be treated as a peripheral player in this strategic landscape. According to the European Commission-supported GSP Hub, 46.1 per cent of Bangladesh's exports went to the EU market in 2024. In other words, a substantial part of Bangladesh's economic future already lies beyond the three major power centres. Market access, product standards, labour rights, and environmentally sustainable production should therefore remain at the heart of Bangladesh's relationship with Europe.

Beyond the European market, Southeast Asia offers opportunities to integrate into nearby production and supply chains. Bangladesh must expand its engagement with this region beyond labour migration and formal diplomatic visits to encompass manufacturing, trade, and knowledge-based cooperation. However, treating ASEAN as a single bloc with uniform interests would make its limitations more apparent than its potential.

What is needed are targeted programmes based on each country's capabilities and Bangladesh's specific needs: port efficiency, investment management, and commercial dispute resolution with Singapore; skilled employment and worker protection with Malaysia; and integration into manufacturing networks, food processing, and market expansion with Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam. Cooperation in digital services and universities could provide these relationships with a long-term foundation. In assessing Vietnam's experience, Bangladesh should look not only at the volume of foreign investment but also at the participation of local suppliers and opportunities for technology transfer and learning.

Relations with the Gulf countries also require the same degree of strategic depth. Beyond sending workers and purchasing energy, Bangladesh should build shared interests in food processing, renewable energy, and investment in productive industries. However, the expansion of economic cooperation will be meaningful only when fair wages, workplace safety, and legal protection for migrant workers become central issues in bilateral discussions. It is impossible to claim that these relationships have strategic depth while keeping the rights of the very workers whose labour forms one of their principal foundations at the margins of diplomacy.

It would also be strategically short-sighted to regard Africa and Latin America as distant geographies. However, declaring vast regions collectively as ‘promising markets’ cannot substitute for proper analysis. Bangladesh needs to identify a select number of countries and assess their demand for pharmaceuticals, light engineering products, agricultural technology, education, and digital services. At the same time, it must examine payment risks, transportation costs, and local regulatory requirements. Entering new markets requires more than political goodwill; it also demands commercial intelligence, credit protection, and reliable local partners.

However, expanding the list of partners does not automatically reduce the risks of dependence. Replacing one lender with five does little to strengthen national capacity if the projects themselves are ineffective. That is why five questions must be answered before undertaking any major partnership: What is the actual economic return after accounting for costs and environmental impacts? How much will dependence increase? Will the country gain access to technology and skills? Are alternatives available in times of crisis? And how transparent is the decision-making process?

The commercial use of a port, operational rights, and military access are separate matters, each requiring distinct conditions. In digital infrastructure, data control and security must be carefully assessed. For defence equipment, diversification of suppliers must go hand in hand with guarantees of maintenance, training, and interoperability. Clear agreements, rather than vague assurances, establish the boundaries of national interests and help address the concerns of partner countries.

To translate this assessment into action, Bangladesh should begin with a limited number of priorities. Over the next five years, it could set measurable targets for developing several new export markets, securing technology partnerships in selected industries, and establishing alternative energy supply arrangements. The ministries and institutions responsible for foreign affairs, commerce, finance, energy, and security must work within a common strategic framework.

Success should be measured not by the number of official visits or memorandums of understanding signed, but by tangible investment, export growth, skills development, and reduced dependence. Rather than waiting for sweeping regional declarations, Bangladesh can begin with smaller but practical and implementable initiatives alongside willing partners.

Beyond economic cooperation, another way for Bangladesh to expand its international influence is through issue-based coalitions. Countries with shared interests can be brought together on issues such as climate reparations, migrant rights, the equitable sharing of responsibilities for refugees, and the management of marine resources. The case brought by The Gambia before the International Court of Justice over allegations of genocide against the Rohingya is a significant example. It demonstrates that even a country with limited territory or military strength can take meaningful initiatives by invoking international law.

Ultimately, the sustainability of these initiatives will depend on Bangladesh's domestic capabilities. The foundations of external independence must be built at home. A weak banking system, opaque procurement processes, and unpredictable policies can prevent even a wide network of partners from becoming genuine alternatives. In such circumstances, urgent needs for loans, markets, and political support narrow the country's bargaining space. Institutional credibility, therefore, is also an asset of foreign policy.

The goal for Bangladesh in the years ahead should not be to maintain an ideal distance from the three major powers, but to develop the capabilities necessary to cooperate with each of them while retaining the freedom to make its own decisions when necessary. The question for the future should be: Which relationships strengthen our production capacity, knowledge, security, and the dignity of our people?

* AKM Ahsan Ullah is a Professor in the Department of International Security and Migration, Universiti Brunei Darussalam, Brunei.

Met Gala unveils new theme after Galliano controversy
item.description:
New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art on Thursday announced a new theme for the exhibition accompanying its prestigious annual Met Gala, after scrapping a planned retrospective of British designer John Galliano amid controversy over his past anti-Semitic remarks.

Running from 9 May, 2027, to 9 January, 2028, the exhibition, titled extraORDINARY, "will examine how design reveals unexpected possibilities within everyday things," the renowned New York museum said in a press release.

The exhibition was initially planned as a retrospective of Galliano, but the designer and the museum announced in late August that it would not go ahead, following criticism from donors and political figures over the fashion designer's past comments.

Stars shine at Met Gala, fashion's biggest night

"After much reflection and discussion with all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time," Galliano, 65, wrote on Instagram then.

"I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry," he added.

Galliano, who served as creative director of Christian Dior from 1996 to 2011 and is widely regarded as one of his generation's most talented designers, saw his career collapse after making antisemitic remarks to customers at a Paris bar.

He was subsequently convicted by a French court over the incident.

Shah Rukh Khan makes Met Gala debut in all-black Sabyasachi suit

After a period of rehabilitation and personal work, he found a new home at the discreet but influential fashion house Maison Margiela.

He served as the label's creative director for a decade, leaving in 2024.

In March 2026, he announced a two-year artistic partnership with Spanish fashion retailer Zara.

The Met's annual Costume Institute exhibition is largely funded by its star-studded gala, which draws leading figures from fashion and entertainment. The 2027 edition of the event is scheduled for 3 May.

"The ordinary is never quite as simple as it appears," said Andrew Bolton, curator at the Met's Costume Institute. "A pair of jeans, a white shirt, or a sweatshirt can hold traces of a life-the habits, memories, and attachments that make something our own."

BCS candidate slashed by muggers in Mohammadpur, phone and wallet snatched
item.description:
Mohammad Tanvir Rahman, 29, was on his way to the Dhaka University area to discuss preparation for the Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examinations with friends and seniors.

He had set out from Atibazar in Keraniganj for this purpose. But as soon as he reached Mohammadpur, he fell victim to muggers.

When the muggers tried to snatch his mobile phone and wallet, Tanvir resisted. They then attacked him with machetes, striking him several times before fleeing with his phone and cash.

The incident took place at around 1:30pm on Tuesday beneath the footbridge beside Allah Karim Mosque, near the bus stand area in Mohammadpur, in the capital. Tanvir was rescued and taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he is currently receiving treatment. However, his machete injuries are not very serious.

Tanvir qualified for a non-cadre position in the 43rd BCS examination. While waiting to join the job, he had also been continuing his preparations for the BCS examinations. He graduated from Noakhali Science and Technology University. His home is in the Atibazar area of Keraniganj.

Tanvir's elder brother, Md Hasan Sarkar, told Prothom Alo that Tanvir had set out from Atibazar around noon, heading towards the Dhaka University area via Bosila Bridge. He was supposed to discuss BCS preparations with friends and seniors there.

When he reached the area beneath the footbridge near Mohammadpur Bus Stand, three to four muggers surrounded him. Each of them was carrying a machete or another sharp weapon.

Hasan said the muggers initially tried to snatch Tanvir's mobile phone and wallet. When he resisted, they began attacking him. They struck him 12 to 14 times on his right hand and back. However, the machete wounds were not very deep.

Although there were people nearby, no one came forward to rescue him out of fear. At one point, when Tanvir fell to the ground, the muggers fled. With the help of some local residents, he was later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Hasan said the muggers took Tanvir's iPhone 16 Pro Max and wallet. The wallet contained Tk 6,000 to Tk 7,000. He said they would go to the police station after completing Tanvir's treatment.

Over the years, the nature of crime in Mohammadpur has changed. New criminal gangs have emerged. Criminal activities and the operations of these gangs continue, and their presence has increased compared with the past.

According to Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) data, around 50 criminal gangs are currently active in Mohammadpur. Of these, 17 are major gangs, each comprising 15 to 20 members.

item.title: Trump's close ties to Nvidia's Huang scrutinised after foreign intelligence concerns
item.description:
NVIDIA-PROBE/TRUMP

US President Donald Trump's close relationship with Nvidia NVDA.OCEO Jensen Huang came under renewed scrutiny on Monday, after the company said its board was investigating whether the tech executive has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Huang is one of Trump's closest allies in Silicon Valley, and the relationship between the two dates to at least 2025. Over the past two years, he has repeatedly voiced support for the administration's agenda and become a regular presence in Washington as Nvidia sought to sell advanced chips to the Chinese market.

Advanced chips are the backbone of the US AI boom and government officials have previously tried to restrict China's access to them through export controls to stifle its AI capabilities.

Nvidia's board launched its probe after a New York Times report said Huang had a close relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who US intelligence officials believe passed information to the Chinese government. Nvidia shares closed down more than four per cent on Monday.

"I’m pushing to investigate Jensen Huang and Nvidia to determine whether our national security was compromised," said Senator Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat, in a post on X. "We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration, who's making these decisions, and who's really got their hand on the wheel."

Democrats on the House of Representatives Foreign Affairs Committee wrote to US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, calling on the Commerce Department to halt exports of advanced AI chips to China.

Nvidia launches investigation into CEO amid reports China spied on him

US Representatives Gabe Amo, Gregory Meeks and Sydney Kamlager-Dove sought answers by December 1 on whether top officials at the Commerce Department were aware of US intelligence linking Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed who is not related to the Nvidia CEO, to Chinese efforts to obtain Nvidia chips.

They also asked in their letter whether the top officials communicated with Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding Alice Huang and Megaspeed.

"If Commerce was not briefed, we need to know why. If it was briefed, we need to know how it responded. And if the Department knowingly permitted these exports despite credible national-security concerns, the American people deserve an explanation," the letter added.

Jensen Huang, the Nvidia CEO, has a direct line to the US president. A Reuters reporter saw Huang's full name pop up on Trump's phone in December 2025.

Huang flew with Trump to China on Air Force One in May, the first visit by a US president to China in nearly a decade. Huang attended a high-profile state dinner in September for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House. The company committed $25 million for Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to media reports.

The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed on Huang's relationship with the woman and on intelligence that she was giving information to the Chinese government, and that he chose not to act on the information.

The White House press office on Monday declined to comment further on Trump's relationship with Huang.

Trump said on Monday the FBI was looking into the Nvidia CEO's affair with the Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Trump said he had spoken to the CEO, who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy. Trump said he believed the CEO.

China's foreign ministry said the spy accusations were "groundless." Reuters could not determine Alice Huang's location to seek comment from her on Monday.

Huang's relationship with Trump has coincided with several favorable policy developments for the company. In April 2025, the administration backed off plans to restrict exports of certain Nvidia AI chips to China after Huang attended a dinner at Trump's Mar-a-Lago club in Florida.

In December 2025, Trump said the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors, its second-best AI chips, to China and collect a 25 per cent fee on such sales.

Trump has lavished Huang with praise, awarding him the nation's highest honor for scientific achievement in October. The same day Trump gave Huang the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million in Nvidia stock during the summer.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Reuters at the time that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio.

item.title: Five more die from measles-like symptoms
item.description:
Five more people died from measles-like symptoms on Tuesday, bringing the total number of deaths from such symptoms to 1,184 as of March 15.
No one died from confirmed measles in the last 24 hours. However, a total of 105 people have died from confirmed measles since March 15, said a daily report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
It said 1,444 people were identified as having measles-like symptoms or confirmed measles across the country, while 1,357 patients with measles-like symptoms were identified in the last 24 hours.
The total number of measles-like cases stood at 241,556 since March 15.
The number of confirmed measles cases in the last 24 hours was 87, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 24,610.
Since March 15, a total of 215,540 patients with measles-like symptoms have been admitted to hospitals. Of them, 206,799 recovered and were discharged from hospitals.

item.title: Whip calls for halt to Baul music events in Habiganj
item.description:
National Parliament Whip and Habiganj MP GK Gouse has asked the administration to remain alert to prevent Baul music and rural folk music events in the district, triggering mixed reactions on social media.
He also called for strict action against obscenity in the name of religious gatherings, music programmes, trade fairs and industrial fairs.
Gouse gave the instructions at a district law and order committee meeting on Sunday. A video of his remarks has since circulated on social media.
“People in this area practise religion and do not like these rural music programmes,” he said, asking the administration to ensure that such events were not held across the district or, at least, in his constituency.
He also urged officials to scrutinise the nature and activities of events before granting permission, warning against activities that could undermine the social and religious environment.
The meeting was chaired by Deputy Commissioner Dr GM Sarfaraz, with Civil Surgeon Ratnadeep Biswas, Superintendent of Police Tarek Mahmud and other committee members in attendance.
His remarks drew criticism from social media users, who argued that Baul music, pala gaan and jatra pala are integral parts of the region's folk heritage.
Mahmud Kha, in a Facebook post, questioned whether an elected representative should restrict people's cultural practices, saying any obscene or unlawful activity could be addressed under existing laws without banning music events altogether.
Another user, Abdul Karim, questioned why police permission should be required to organise music programmes, arguing that law enforcers should intervene only if an event involves obscene or inappropriate content.
The district administration's response to the criticism could not be obtained. Deputy Commissioner Dr GM Sarfaraz Hossain did not answer calls seeking comment.

item.title: ICT chief prosecutor: No legal scope to issue passport to fugitive Hasina
item.description:
Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Md Aminul Islam has said the government has no legal authority to issue a passport or travel document to former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, a death-row convict who is currently staying in India.
“If she wishes to return to Bangladesh, she must do so under the Extradition Treaty,” he told reporters on the ICT premises on Tuesday.
Responding to questions about discussions over issuing Hasina a passport or travel pass, Aminul cited Articles 6 and 7 of the Bangladesh Passport Order, 1973, which he said bar such a move.
Under Article 6, passport authorities cannot issue a passport to anyone convicted of an offence and sentenced to at least two years in prison within the five years preceding an application. Article 7 empowers the government to impound or revoke the passport of anyone convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude.
“Crimes against humanity fall squarely under the definition of moral turpitude,” the chief prosecutor said, adding that Hasina’s passport had already been revoked.
He also argued that constitutional protections relating to freedom of movement could not be invoked by an absconding convict who had evaded trial.
Hasina had ignored arrest warrants and notices published in newspapers and did not participate in the proceedings, Aminul said. He added that she had also failed to appeal against the tribunal’s verdict within the stipulated 30-day period.
Issuing her a passport or travel document, he said, would undermine the judicial process.
On Hasina’s stay in India, the chief prosecutor said the Indian government had stated that she was given shelter on humanitarian grounds. He added that his office had no information about any formal written request from Hasina to the Indian authorities seeking permission to return to Bangladesh.
Had she genuinely wanted to return, she could have faced the trial or surrendered within the 30-day appeal period, he said.
Aminul described recent discussions about her possible return as political posturing, reiterating that she could return only through the formal extradition process.

item.title: Awami League activists block Padma Bridge approach road
item.description:
Awami League activists and its student wing, Chhatra League, blocked the Dhaka-Bhanga Expressway near the Padma Bridge toll plaza in Zajira, Shariatpur, carrying oars and chanting slogans including “Joy Bangla” and “Joy Bangabandhu”.
Several crude bombs exploded and two trucks were vandalised during the blockade, leaving hundreds of vehicles stranded on and around the bridge for nearly an hour, reports Bangla Tribune.
The incident took place in the Nawdoba area of Zajira Upazila between 1:30am and 2:30am on Tuesday, following a gathering late Monday.
According to local residents and police, around 700-800 people assembled in the area and later took positions on the expressway in front of the toll plaza. Police said several explosions occurred and two parked trucks were vandalised.
The blockade halted traffic between Dhaka and the southwestern region in both directions, causing long tailbacks on the bridge and nearby roads.
Members of Padma Bridge South Police Station, Shibchar Highway Police and district police later reached the scene and dispersed the protesters. Traffic subsequently returned to normal. No one was arrested, police said.
Shibchar Highway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Enamul Hasan said additional police personnel, along with members of the highway police and Padma Bridge South Police Station, conducted a joint operation to clear the road.
The protest came ahead of a nationwide blockade announced by the Chhatra League on Facebook for Tuesday. Reports of activists gathering in different parts of Shariatpur had circulated a day earlier.
On Monday evening, police conducted a drive in Nawdoba and seized 500 packets of khichuri from a business establishment. The Shariatpur district unit of Jubo Dal later held a protest procession in the area.
Mahsin Madbar, convener of the Shariatpur district Chhatra League, was seen addressing the overnight gathering. A video of his speech circulating on Facebook shows him saying they would resist any attempt to obstruct BNP programmes.
The incident caused panic among passengers, as the blockade and explosions occurred near the Padma Bridge South Police Station, a cantonment, the bridge service area and the toll plaza.

item.title: Sifat murder case: Further investigation report due on Dec 14
item.description:
A Dhaka court has set December 14 for submission of a further investigation report in a case over the killing of Md Sifat Hossain, 26, during the July 2024 uprising.
The case names former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and 25 others.
The date was fixed on Monday after the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), the agency assigned to conduct the further investigation, failed to submit its report. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order.
Sub-Inspector Rafiqul Islam of the prosecution department confirmed the development.
Sifat’s father, Kamal Howlader, filed the case against Hasina and 21 others at a Dhaka court on August 15, 2024. The court recorded his statement and directed Mirpur Model Police Station to register the complaint as a case.
Other accused include former ministers Obaidul Quader and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former MPs Kamal Ahmed Majumder, Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil and Salahuddin Mahmud (SM) Zahid, former inspector general of police Abdullah Al Mamun, former DB chief Harun Or Rashid, former additional joint commissioner Biplob Kumar, and former Dhaka Metropolitan Police commissioner Habibur Rahman.
On May 28, Mirpur Model Police Station Sub-Inspector Mizanur Rahman submitted a charge sheet against Hasina and 25 others after completing the investigation. However, Sifat’s father was dissatisfied that two accused, Jiaul Haque Zia and Mehedi Hasan, had been excluded from the case.
On September 1, Kamal Howlader filed a no-confidence petition against the police report, alleging that the investigating officer had submitted a biased charge sheet without properly considering the allegations or visiting the crime scene.
After hearing the petition on October 5, the court ordered the PBI to conduct a further investigation.
According to the case statement, thousands of students and members of the public were taking part in the quota reform movement in front of MS Power in Senpara, Mirpur-10, on July 20, 2024, when police opened fire indiscriminately.
Sifat was crossing the road to reach a safe place when he was shot. The bullet entered one side of his head and exited through the other, killing him, the complaint says.

item.title: Chhatra League locks JU main gate
item.description:
Activists of the activities-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League locked the main gate of Jahangirnagar University (JU), known as Dairy Gate, late Monday.
Witnesses and university administration sources said a group of 10-12 activists put a lock on the gate before leaving the scene. The move was reportedly part of the organisation’s nationwide lockdown program announced for Tuesday.
JU Proctor Prof Dr Abdul Halim said the activists threatened security guards while locking the gate in the dead of night.
Although police were patrolling nearby, the group completed the act and fled within a minute, he added.
The university administration informed Savar police, Savar Circle, Ashulia police, the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) and other law enforcement and intelligence agencies about the incident.
Meanwhile, a video circulated on social media after the incident, urging JU teachers and students to stay home in solidarity with the nationwide student strike announced for Tuesday.
The video also called for the program’s success, citing demands for educational rights, democracy, freedom and people's rights.

item.title: Barguna sees overnight arson, roadblocks and lockouts
item.description:
Several government and private institutions in Barguna, including educational establishments, upazila parishad, municipal and union parishad offices, were locked overnight, while a truck was set on fire and attempts were made to torch a bus.
Activists of the activities-banned Chhatra League have been blamed for the incidents, which took place in Barguna Sadar, Betagi, Patharghata and Bamna from Monday night.
Local sources said locks were put on Barguna Zilla School, Government Girls’ High School and several other educational institutions. The Betagi Upazila Parishad building was locked around 1am on Tuesday.
Around the same time, a municipal truck was set on fire in front of the Betagi Municipality Office. An attempt was also made to set fire to a bus parked at Betagi bus stand.
Several schools and colleges in Betagi, including Bibichini School and College, Putiakhali Adarsha Secondary School, Hossanabad Adarsha Secondary School, Mokamia Secondary School, Kaunia Emdadia Secondary School and Zamir Uddin Secondary School, were also locked. The Hossanabad and Mokamia union parishad offices were similarly locked.
Posters bearing the name of Betagi Upazila Chhatra League General Secretary Sifat Sikder were found at the institutions.
In another incident, tree trunks were placed across the Barguna-Barisal regional highway at the Chandkhali bypass, obstructing traffic. Barguna Government College in Patharghata and Ramna Sher-e-Bangla Adarsha Secondary School in Bamna were also locked.
Barguna Additional Superintendent of Police (Administration and Finance) Mukit Hasan Khan said police had visited the affected locations and educational institutions.
“All the locks have been removed, and the situation is now normal,” he said, adding that several activists of Chhatra League had been arrested.
Police are conducting operations to identify and arrest others involved in the acts of sabotage and disorder, he added.

item.title: Five unexploded crude bombs hurled at Rangpur bus stand
item.description:
Five crude bombs were hurled at Mithapukur bus stand in Rangpur on Monday night in support of a strike called by Chhatra League.
The bombs were thrown one after another from the bus stand overpass on the Dhaka-Rangpur highway around 11pm, police said. None exploded, and no casualties or damage were reported, although the incident triggered panic in the area.
Police and witnesses said the attackers fled immediately after throwing the devices. Police later recovered all five unexploded bombs and defused them.
The devices were made using jorda containers wrapped in tape, police said.
Security was tightened around the bus stand and along the Dhaka-Rangpur highway following the incident.
Mithapukur Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ruhul Amin confirmed the recovery of the five unexploded bombs, saying police operations were underway to identify and arrest those responsible.
He said further details might be available by Tuesday evening.

item.title: Grenade-like objects found at Rajshashi airport, minister escorted out
item.description:
Panic spread after two grenade-like objects were found inside a flower bed beside the main gate of Shah Makhdum Airport in Rajshahi on Tuesday.
A passerby spotted the objects around 11am and alerted police. The airport's main gate was temporarily closed for security reasons, with passengers directed to use an alternative mosque gate.
The objects were later defused by a bomb disposal unit in an open field in Pakuria area of Paba upazila.
According to police, the passerby spotted the objects inside a flower bed on the left side of the airport's main gate and informed Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Palash, who was in charge of the Romeo-81 patrol vehicle of the Baya Police Outpost under Airport Police Station.
ASI Palash immediately informed the officer-in-charge of Airport Police Station. Police and airport authorities rushed to the scene and tightened security.
The airport's main gate was closed, and the mosque gate was opened as an alternative entrance and exit for passengers, triggering panic among those arriving at the airport.
Members of the Armed Police Battalion (APBn), responsible for security at the main gate, also took up alert positions. Police said three armed APBn members were on duty there at the time.
However, it was not immediately clear who had left the objects at the site.
Meanwhile, Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku was inside the airport's VIP lounge when the incident occurred.
He arrived in Rajshahi on a flight at 10:50am while travelling from Dhaka to Bogra, making a stop in Rajshahi.
After news of the suspicious objects spread, authorities also considered his security. Police informed him about the situation and escorted him out through the airport's rear gate instead of the main entrance.
He then left for Bogra by road.
Rajshahi Metropolitan Police Additional Deputy Commissioner (Media) Md Gaziur Rahman said police quickly reached the scene after receiving reports of two grenade-like objects near the airport's main gate.
Necessary measures were taken in coordination with airport authorities and security personnel. The main gate was temporarily closed, and alternative access was arranged to ensure the safety of passengers and the public.
The objects were later defused by the bomb disposal unit in an open field in Pakuria area of Paba upazila.
He added that the actual identity of the objects would be confirmed after examination.
Police are investigating who left the objects near the airport and why.

item.title: Two crude bombs explode at DU campus, private car driver hurt
item.description:
Two crude bomb explosions at separate locations on the Dhaka University (DU) campus on Tuesday left a private car driver injured.
The explosions occurred around 2:20pm near the Shadow area beside the Arts Building and inside the Faculty of Business Studies (FBS).
The injured driver was identified as Sohel, 36.
Eyewitnesses said a man arriving on a motorcycle hurled a crude bomb before fleeing the scene.
DU Proctor Professor Dr Israfil Ratan confirmed the explosions, saying members of the proctorial team rushed to the locations immediately after receiving reports.
No one has been detained in connection with the incident so far.
Asked about casualties, the proctor said the FBS dean had informed him that a vehicle driver was injured in one of the explosions.
